ps.en: When an [[adult]] who was the first in her family to enter university arrived on campus, she did not [[address]] the crowd so much as avoid it. The [[administration]] had promised [[adequate]] housing, yet the real test was whether she could [[adjust]] to a world that felt foreign to her. She would later [[add]] to her worries an [[additional]] fear — that she had become an [[addict]] of the phone she could not put down, and that every [[addition]] to her to-do list pulled her further from sleep.
ps.zh: 当一位全家第一个迈进大学校门的成年人抵达校园时，她没有对着人群讲话，而是避开了他们。校方许诺过充足的宿舍，然而真正的考验是她能否适应一个对她而言全然陌生的世界。后来，她又为自己的焦虑添上一重额外的恐惧——她已成了离不开手机的瘾君子，而待办清单上的每一项新增，都把她更远地拽离睡眠。

ps.en: Her [[admission]] to the college had been the easy part; the harder thing was to [[admit]], quietly, that she missed home more than she had admitted to anyone. She learned to [[adapt]] by joining a club that had decided to [[adopt]] a stray dog from the shelter down the road. There she met a professor she would come to [[admire]], not for his titles but for the way he simply listened.
ps.zh: 被大学录取反倒是最容易的事；更难的是悄悄承认，她对家的思念远胜过向任何人承认的程度。她靠加入一个社团学会了适应——那个社团决定收养路边收容所里的一只流浪狗。在那里，她遇见了一位令她钦佩的教授，不是因为他的头衔，而是因为他只是静静地听。

ps.en: By the end of the first term the adult she had been at the start was someone else entirely. The phone still called, but the addiction no longer owned her evenings, and the additional hours she had won back went to the reading she once thought herself too small for. She wrote home: the place was strange, then bearable, then hers.
ps.zh: 第一学期结束时，当初那个成年人已完全是另一个人。手机仍会呼唤她，但那份瘾不再占据她的夜晚，而她赢回的那些额外时光，都给了曾以为自己读不懂的读物。她写信回家：这个地方先是陌生，接着尚可忍受，最后成了她的。

ps.en: The [[branch]] clinic had run out of the [[brand]] of vaccine it trusted, and the doctor could feel her own [[brain]] beginning to blur with fatigue. She had to [[brace]] herself for the night shift, then [[toss]] a coin to decide which family to see first. By midnight the [[total]] of untreated cases had passed forty, and the corridor smelled of the cold that would not leave.
ps.zh: 那家分部诊所已经用完了它信赖的那个品牌的疫苗，医生能感觉到自己的头脑因疲惫而开始模糊。她得为夜班让自己做好准备，然后抛一枚硬币，决定先接诊哪一家人。到午夜时，未经诊治的病例总数已越过四十，走廊里弥漫着挥之不去的寒意。

ps.en: A [[vicious]] new strain was driving the [[trend]], and every [[victim]] who arrived needed to be [[treated|treat]] at once. She would [[touch]] a child's forehead, make the [[tough]] calls no one else would make, and wonder how a system meant to heal could feel so thin at its edges.
ps.zh: 一种凶恶的新毒株正推动着这一趋势，每一个抵达的受害者都需要立刻得到治疗。她会摸一摸孩子的额头，做出别人都不愿做的艰难决定，并暗自疑惑：一个本为治愈而生的体系，边缘为何会如此单薄。

ps.en: When two hospitals finally signed a [[treaty]] of shared beds, the [[vice]]-director admitted what they all already knew: the line had nearly broken. The doctor went home and, for once, did not check her phone — the ward would wait for no one, but tonight it could wait for her.
ps.zh: 当两家医院终于签署了一份共享病床的协定，那位副院长承认了大家心里都清楚的事：那条线几乎已经绷断。医生回到家中，破天荒地没有去看手机——诊室从不为谁停下，但今晚，它可以为她停一停。

ps.en: The [[code]] was ready, and when the first [[client]] [[clicked|click]] the demo link, the whole room seemed to hold its breath. To [[close]] the contract they had rehearsed for a month, the founder had memorised every number and every silence.
ps.zh: 代码已经就绪，当第一位客户点开演示链接时，整个房间仿佛屏住了呼吸。为了促成那份他们排练了一个月的合同，创始人把每个数字、每一次停顿都背了下来。

ps.en: They had built the product around [[personal]] data, betting that [[personality]] — not price — would win users over. The [[personnel]] team had taken a year to [[form]], and its [[formation]] had been anything but smooth: three quit, two were hired, and one simply vanished.
ps.zh: 他们的产品围绕个人数据而建，押注于「个性而非价格」能赢得用户。人事团队花了一年才组建起来，而它的形成远非顺利：三人离职，两人入职，还有一人凭空消失。

ps.en: The [[formal]] meeting began, the slides in the required [[format]], yet the founder would not [[cling]] to the script. He opened the [[closet]] where the broken prototypes had hidden and showed the client every failure that came before the win — proof, he said, that the team knew what not to repeat.
ps.zh: 正式的会议开始了，幻灯片是按规定格式做的，然而创始人不愿死守讲稿。他打开了那只藏着报废原型的暗柜，把胜利之前的所有失败都展示给客户看——他说，这正是团队懂得不再重蹈覆辙的证据。

ps.en: A [[former]] apprentice returned to the [[guild]] where he had once been afraid of its [[formidable]] master, hoping the old man could still [[guide]] his hand after all these years. The courtyard was smaller than memory, but the smell of oil and wood was exactly the same.
ps.zh: 一位从前的学徒回到了那家行会——他曾在这里畏惧那位令人生畏的师傅，如今只盼着多年以后，老人仍能指导他的手法。庭院比记忆里小，但油与木的气味分毫不差。

ps.en: There was no secret [[formula]], only the discipline to [[formulate]] each step before taking it; under the master's [[guidance]] he followed every [[guideline]] without question. He counted himself [[fortunate]], though his [[fortune]] was measured in time, not money — a year of mornings no one else would have given him.
ps.zh: 并没有什么秘方，只有一种纪律：在动手之前，先把每一步都构想清楚；在师傅的引导下，他不假思索地遵循每一条准则。他觉得自己幸运，尽管他的财富是以时间而非金钱来衡量的——是别人都不会给他的、整整一年的清晨。

ps.en: For years he had carried a quiet [[guilt]], certain he was [[guilty]] of wasting his youth. The [[recognition]] came not as a prize but as a question — could he now [[recognize]] the teacher in himself, and pass on what had once been given freely to him?
ps.zh: 多年来他怀揣着一份无声的内疚，笃信自己浪费了青春、是有罪的。而那份认可并非以奖赏的形式到来，而是一句反问——如今的他，能否在自己身上认出那位老师，并把曾无偿给予他的东西传递下去？

c: a drug addict 吸毒成瘾者
be addicted to 对…上瘾
an Internet addict 网瘾者
words.dif: addict 兼动词「使上瘾」与名词「瘾君子」；addiction 是名词「瘾本身」
words.pat: He became an addict of the phone he could not put down.
words.patZh: 他成了那只放不下的手机瘾君子。

c: add to 增添，增加
add up 合计；说得通
add that... 补充说…
add sth to sth 把…添加到…
words.dif: add 表「添加、补充说」；plus 是介词「加」；increase 侧重「数量增长」
words.pat: She would add to her worries an extra fear of failure.
words.patZh: 她又为自己的焦虑添上一份对失败的额外恐惧。

c: in addition 此外
in addition to 除…之外
a useful addition 有用的补充
an addition to the family 家里新添的人
words.dif: addition 指「增添的人或物」；increase 指「数量的增多」，不说 an increase to the list
words.pat: Every addition to her to-do list pulled her further from sleep.
words.patZh: 待办清单上的每一项新增，都把她更远地拽离睡眠。

c: additional cost 额外成本
additional information 补充信息
an additional hour 额外一小时
additional staff 增援人员
words.dif: additional 强调「额外追加的」，常用于成本、信息、人手；extra 更口语化
words.pat: The additional hours she won back went to the reading she loved.
words.patZh: 她赢回的那些额外时光，都给了她钟爱的阅读。

words.exam: 地址；向…作（正式）讲话；处理
c: address a meeting 在会上讲话
address the issue 处理问题
deliver an address 发表演说
home address 家庭住址
words.dif: address 作动词常考「处理（问题）」与「向…讲话」两义；作名词是「地址、演说」
words.pat: A good leader must address the crowd before acting.
words.patZh: 优秀的领导者必先向众人讲话，再采取行动。

c: adequate housing 充足的住房
adequate to the task 足以胜任该任务
adequate evidence 充分的证据
barely adequate 勉强够
words.dif: adequate 强调「刚好够、恰如其分」；ample 强调「绰绰有余」
words.pat: The administration had promised adequate housing for every freshman.
words.patZh: 校方曾许诺为每位新生提供充足的宿舍。

c: adjust to 适应…
adjust oneself to 使自己适应
adjust the settings 调节设置
adjust prices 调整价格
words.dif: adjust 与 adapt 都表「适应」，但 adjust 更侧重「微调、校准」，adapt 更侧重「根本性改变以契合」
words.pat: It takes time to adjust to a world that feels foreign.
words.patZh: 要适应一个全然陌生的世界，需要时间。

c: under the administration of 在…的管理下
public administration 公共行政
the school administration 学校管理层
an efficient administration 高效的管理层
words.dif: administration 指「管理机构/行政部门」，作集合名词；government 特指「政府」
words.pat: The administration promised adequate housing but delivered little.
words.patZh: 管理层许诺了充足的宿舍，却兑现甚少。

c: admire sb for sth 因…而钦佩某人
deeply admire 深深钦佩
admire one's courage 钦佩某人的勇气
words.dif: admire 兼「钦佩」与「羡慕」；envy 多含「嫉妒」的贬义色彩
words.pat: She came to admire the professor for the way he listened.
words.patZh: 她渐渐因教授倾听的方式而钦佩他。

c: admission to a university 大学录取
gain admission 获得准入
admission of guilt 承认有罪
free admission 免费入场
fam: admit v. 承认；准许进入
words.dif: admission 作「录取/准入」和「承认」两义都考；作「入场券」时近 ticket
words.pat: Her admission to the college had been the easy part.
words.patZh: 被大学录取反倒是最容易的事。

c: admit doing sth 承认做了…
admit to a mistake 承认错误
admit sb to 准许…进入
be admitted to hospital 被收治入院
words.dif: admit 表「承认」时近 acknowledge/confess；表「准入」时近 allow in。介词 to 后接名词或动名词
words.pat: She was reluctant to admit that she missed home.
words.patZh: 她不愿承认自己想家。

c: adapt to 适应…
adapt oneself to 使自己适应
adapt a novel for film 把小说改编成电影
adapt to change 适应变化
words.dif: adapt 与 adjust 近义，但 adapt 可接宾语表「改编（作品）」，adjust 无此用法
words.pat: She learned to adapt by joining a club she liked.
words.patZh: 她靠加入一个喜欢的社团学会了适应。

words.exam: 采用；采纳；正式通过；批准；收养
c: adopt a child 收养孩子
adopt a policy 采纳政策
adopt a suggestion 采纳建议
be adopted as 被正式通过为
words.dif: adopt 四个义项都考（采用/采纳/通过/收养）；词义靠宾语区分，阅读高频
words.pat: The club decided to adopt a stray dog from the shelter.
words.patZh: 社团决定收养收容所里的一只流浪狗。

words.exam: 成年人的；成熟的；成（年）人
c: an adult education 成人教育
a responsible adult 负责任的成年人
reach adulthood 成年
adult life 成年生活
fam: adulterate v. 掺假（同源异义，易混）
words.dif: adult 兼形容词「成年人的」与名词「成年人」；adulterate（掺假）形近但义远
words.pat: She was the first adult in her family to enter university.
words.patZh: 她是家里第一个迈进大学的成年人。

c: brace oneself for 为…做好准备
brace against the wind 顶着风站稳
a brace for the leg 腿部支架
brace the door 撑住门
words.dif: brace 作动词常考「使做好准备（迎接冲击）」，作名词表「支架、托架」
words.pat: She had to brace herself for the long night shift.
words.patZh: 她得为漫长的夜班让自己做好准备。

c: use one's brain 动脑筋
brain drain 人才流失
brain injury 脑损伤
rack one's brains 绞尽脑汁
words.dif: brain 口语常指「脑力、智能」（use your brain）；mind 更侧重「心智、思维」
words.pat: She could feel her own brain blurring with fatigue.
words.patZh: 她能感觉到自己的头脑因疲惫而开始模糊。

c: a branch office 分部办事处
a branch of science 学科分支
the branch of a river 支流
branch out 拓展新领域
words.dif: branch 可指「树枝、分部、学科分支、支流」，作动词表「拓展（新业务）」
words.pat: The branch clinic had run out of the vaccine it trusted.
words.patZh: 那家分部诊所已用完了它信赖的疫苗。

words.exam: 商标；标记；打烙印；使铭记
c: a famous brand 知名品牌
brand loyalty 品牌忠诚度
brand sb as 给某人打上…的烙印
brand a product 给产品打商标
words.dif: brand 作名词是「品牌、商标」，作动词可表「打烙印」或「使铭记（负面）」
words.pat: The clinic ran out of the brand of vaccine it trusted.
words.patZh: 诊所用完了它信赖的那个品牌的疫苗。

c: toss a coin 抛硬币
toss aside 随手扔到一边
toss and turn 翻来覆去
toss a salad 拌沙拉
fam: toss-up n. 难以预料的事
words.dif: toss 比 throw 随意、幅度小，常指「轻轻抛、随手扔」；toss a coin 是固定搭配
words.pat: She tossed a coin to decide which family to see first.
words.patZh: 她抛硬币决定先接诊哪一家人。

c: a total of 总共
in total 总计
the total amount 总额
total up to 合计为
words.dif: total 强调「加总后的全部」，可作名词（总数）、形容词（总的）与动词（合计达）；sum 侧重「金额、款项」
words.pat: By midnight the total of untreated cases had passed forty.
words.patZh: 到午夜时，未经诊治的病例总数已越过四十。

c: touch sb's hand 触碰某人的手
touch on 提及，涉及
a touching story 感人故事
keep in touch 保持联系
words.dif: touch 的多义极多（碰/涉及/触动/少许），阅读常考「涉及（touch on）」与「触动人心」
words.pat: She would touch a child's forehead and make the call.
words.patZh: 她会摸一摸孩子的额头，然后做出判断。

words.exam: 坚韧的；强硬的；艰苦的；棘手的
c: a tough decision 艰难的决定
a tough negotiator 强硬的谈判者
tough times 艰苦时期
a tough problem 棘手的问题
words.dif: tough 在考研中常不译「坚韧」而译「艰难、棘手、强硬」，靠搭配定义
words.pat: She made the tough calls no one else would make.
words.patZh: 她做出了别人都不愿做的艰难决定。

c: treat a patient 治疗病人
treat sb fairly 公平对待某人
treat a subject 论述课题
a treat 一份款待
fam: treaty n. 条约（同源异义）
words.dif: treat 四义都考（对待/处理/治疗/款待）；treaty（条约）形近但义远，易混
words.pat: Every victim who arrived needed to be treated at once.
words.patZh: 每个抵达的受害者都需要立刻得到治疗。

c: sign a treaty 签署条约
a peace treaty 和平条约
under the treaty 根据条约
a treaty of alliance 同盟条约
fam: treat v. 对待；治疗（同源异义）
words.dif: treaty 指「正式的条约、协定」，多用于国家间；agreement 泛指任何协议
words.pat: Two hospitals signed a treaty of shared beds.
words.patZh: 两家医院签署了一份共享病床的协定。

c: a rising trend 上升趋势
the trend of events 事态的动向
set a trend 引领潮流
against the trend 逆势
words.dif: trend 与 tendency 近义；trend 更强调「可观察的走向、潮流」，tendency 侧重「内在倾向」
words.pat: A vicious strain was driving the upward trend.
words.patZh: 一种凶恶的毒株正推动着上升的趋势。

c: a vice-president 副总统；副总裁
a vice of character 性格上的缺点
grip like a vice 死死夹住
vices and virtues 恶习与美德
words.dif: vice 作名词常考「恶习、缺点」，作形容词表「副的」（vice-chairman）；vicious 是「凶恶的」
words.pat: The vice-director admitted what they all already knew.
words.patZh: 那位副院长承认了大家心里都清楚的事。

c: a vicious circle 恶性循环
a vicious attack 凶狠的攻击
vicious gossip 恶毒的流言
a vicious dog 恶犬
words.dif: vicious 强调「凶残、恶毒」，常用于 vicious circle（恶性循环）这一固定搭配
words.pat: A vicious new strain was driving the trend.
words.patZh: 一种凶恶的新毒株正推动着这一趋势。

c: a victim of 的受害者
fall victim to 成为…的牺牲品
an innocent victim 无辜的受害者
aid the victims 救助受害者
words.dif: victim 是「受害者、牺牲品」；casualty 是「伤亡者」，侧重事故或战争中的死伤
words.pat: Every victim who arrived needed to be treated at once.
words.patZh: 每个抵达的受害者都需要立刻得到治疗。

words.exam: 点击；发出咔嗒声；突然明白
c: click the link 点击链接

a mouse click 一次鼠标点击

words.pat: The client clicked the demo link and the room held its breath.

c: a regular client 常客

words.pat: He opened the closet where the broken prototypes had hidden.
words.patZh: 他打开了那只藏着报废原型的暗柜。

break a code 破译密码

words.dif: code 三义都考（代码/密码/法典）；coding 指「编程」，法律语境下 code 是「法典」
words.pat: The code was ready, and the demo ran without a hitch.
words.patZh: 代码已经就绪，演示顺畅无阻。

c: personal data 个人数据
a personal letter 私人信件
personal experience 亲身经历
personal attack 人身攻击
words.dif: personal 表「个人的、私人的」；personnel 是「人事、全体人员」，只差一个字母，极易混
words.pat: They built the product around personal data and user trust.
words.patZh: 他们的产品围绕个人数据与用户信任而建。

c: a strong personality 鲜明的个性
personality clash 性格冲突
brand personality 品牌个性
a TV personality 电视名人
words.dif: personality 是「个性、人格」；personnel 是「人员、人事」，拼写相近但义完全不同
words.pat: They bet that personality, not price, would win users.
words.patZh: 他们押注于个性而非价格能赢得用户。

c: personnel department 人事部门
medical personnel 医务人员
a shortage of personnel 人手短缺
personnel manager 人事经理
words.dif: personnel 是集合名词「全体人员、人事」，谓语用复数；personal 是形容词「个人的」，二者形近必混
words.pat: The personnel team had taken a year to form.
words.patZh: 人事团队花了一年才组建起来。

c: form a team 组建团队
form a habit 养成习惯
in the form of 以…的形式
fill in a form 填表格
words.dif: form 作动词常考「组成、形成、养成（习惯）」；作名词表「形式、表格」
words.pat: The personnel team took a year to form and stabilise.
words.patZh: 人事团队花了一年才组建并稳定下来。

c: a formal meeting 正式会议
formal education 正规教育
formal dress 礼服
a formal apology 正式道歉
words.dif: formal 表「正式的、合乎程序的」；casual 是其反义「随意的」
words.pat: The formal meeting began with the slides on screen.
words.patZh: 正式的会议以屏幕上的幻灯片开场。

words.exam: 设计；安排；格式；使格式化
c: in the required format 按规定格式
the format of a meeting 会议安排
a new format 新形式
format a disk 格式化磁盘
words.dif: format 作名词是「格式、版式、安排」，作动词表「格式化、编排」
words.pat: The slides were in the required format, nothing missing.
words.patZh: 幻灯片按规定格式制作，毫无遗漏。

c: the formation of a team 团队的组建
cloud formation 云层结构
in formation 排成队形
the formation of a habit 习惯的养成
words.dif: formation 是 form 的名词，表「形成、组建（过程）」；强调从无到有的过程
words.pat: Its formation had been anything but smooth.
words.patZh: 它的组建远非顺利。

c: the former... the latter... 前者…后者…
a former student 昔日的学生
former times 往昔
my former boss 我前任老板
words.dif: former 与 latter 成对（前者/后者）；ex- 作前缀也表「前任的」，如 ex-president
words.pat: A former apprentice returned to the guild he once feared.
words.patZh: 一位从前的学徒回到了他曾经畏惧的那家行会。

words.exam: 令人敬畏的；可怕的；难以应付的
c: a formidable opponent 难缠的对手
a formidable task 艰巨的任务
a formidable master 令人生畏的师傅
a formidable challenge 严峻的挑战
words.dif: formidable 强调「因强大/艰巨而令人敬畏或怯步」，不是单纯「可怕的」
words.pat: He had once been afraid of its formidable master.
words.patZh: 他曾经畏惧那位令人生畏的师傅。

c: a secret formula 秘方
a winning formula 制胜公式
the formula for success 成功之道
a chemical formula 化学式
fam: formulate v. 构想；系统地阐述
words.dif: formula 除「公式」外，常表「固定程式、秘诀」（a winning formula）；复数 formulae/formulas
words.pat: There was no secret formula, only daily discipline.
words.patZh: 并没有什么秘方，只有日复一日的纪律。

words.exam: 规划；构想出；系统地阐述
c: formulate a plan 构想出计划
formulate a policy 制定政策
formulate an idea 系统阐述想法
formulate a theory  formulate 理论
words.dif: formulate 强调「经思考后系统构拟/表述」，近 devise/draft；form 是更简单的「形成」
words.pat: He learned to formulate each step before taking it.
words.patZh: 他学会了在动手之前先把每一步都构想清楚。

c: be fortunate in 在…方面幸运
a fortunate coincidence 幸运的巧合
fortunate enough to 足够幸运得以…
less fortunate 境况较差的
words.dif: fortunate 与 lucky 近义，但 fortunate 更正式，且可接 in/that 从句
words.pat: He counted himself fortunate, though his fortune was time.
words.patZh: 他觉得自己幸运，尽管他的财富是时间。

c: make a fortune 发财
tell sb's fortune 给人算命
a small fortune 一大笔钱
by good fortune 幸运地
words.dif: fortune 兼「运气、命运」与「大笔钱财」两义，阅读中常考后者（make a fortune 发财）
words.pat: His fortune was measured in time, not money.
words.patZh: 他的财富是以时间而非金钱来衡量的。

c: guide sb through 引导某人度过
a tour guide 导游
a guide to 的指南
guide one's hand 指导某人的手法
words.dif: guide 作动词表「指引、引导」；作名词是「导游、指南」。近 direct/lead
words.pat: He hoped the old man could still guide his hand.
words.patZh: 他盼着老人仍能指导他的手法。

c: under one's guidance 在…的引导下
career guidance 职业指导
seek guidance 寻求指点
moral guidance 道德指引
words.dif: guidance 是不可数名词「指导、引导」；guide 可作可数「导游、指南」
words.pat: Under the master's guidance he followed every rule.
words.patZh: 在师傅的引导下，他遵循每一条规矩。

words.exam: 指导方针；指导原则；准则
c: follow a guideline 遵循准则
set guidelines 制定指导方针
break the guidelines 违反准则
design guidelines 设计规范
words.dif: guideline 是「准则、指导方针」，比 rule 柔和，常用于政策与规范语境
words.pat: He followed every guideline without question.
words.patZh: 他不假思索地遵循每一条准则。

c: a trade guild 行业公会
join a guild 加入行会
the guild of craftsmen 工匠行会
a journalists' guild 记者协会
fam: gild v. 镀金（形近异义）
words.dif: guild 指「（中世纪的）行会、同业公会」，今泛指行业协会；gild（镀金）形近义远
words.pat: He returned to the guild where he had once trained.
words.patZh: 他回到了自己曾经学艺的那家行会。

c: a sense of guilt 内疚感
burdened by guilt 被内疚折磨
admit guilt 承认罪责
guilt by association 株连
fam: guilty adj. 有罪的；内疚的
words.dif: guilt 是「内疚、罪责」；shame 是「羞耻」，侧重丢脸而非自责
words.pat: For years he carried a quiet guilt about his youth.
words.patZh: 多年来他怀揣着一份对青春的无声内疚。

c: be guilty of 犯有…罪；对…感到内疚
feel guilty about 对…感到内疚
plead guilty 认罪
a guilty conscience 内疚的良心
words.dif: guilty 后接 of，兼「有罪的」与「内疚的」；innocent（无罪的）是其反义
words.pat: He was certain he was guilty of wasting his youth.
words.patZh: 他笃信自己浪费了青春、是有罪的。

c: win recognition 赢得认可
beyond recognition 认不出来
in recognition of 为表彰…
facial recognition 人脸识别
words.dif: recognition 兼「认出」与「认可、表彰」；作「认不出」常用 beyond recognition
words.pat: The recognition came not as a prize but as a question.
words.patZh: 那份认可并非以奖赏的形式到来，而是一句反问。

c: recognize sb as 承认某人是…
recognize a face 认出一张脸
recognize the truth 承认事实
be recognized for 因…而受认可
words.dif: recognize 后接 as 表「承认某人为…」；identify 强调「辨认、确认身份」
words.pat: Could he now recognize the teacher in himself?
words.patZh: 如今的他，能否在自己身上认出那位老师？
